criteria: Down 20%+ since the flagged earnings report, market cap over $1B, RSI under 30, a real recent earnings miss (or swing to a loss), gross margin still positive and revenue not collapsing (down under 25% YoY, not declining 3+ of the last 4 quarters), excludes banks, pharma, and biotech. Ranked by Reset Score (0 to 100), recomputed daily from live price against the original earnings shock and leadership finding: earnings shock size, price drop severity, a confirmed recent leadership change as a bonus signal, and how well the underlying financial health is actually verified. Cards persist day to day once listed and only drop off once the reset has clearly played out or a genuine new health concern is confirmed, never just for the price falling further.
disclaimer: Informational screener only, not investment advice. Data from live market feed. Not a recommendation to buy or sell any security.

cards.name: Nayax
cards.why: Runs a global payments and commerce platform. Wall Street had penciled in a profit this quarter; instead the company swung to an outright loss, and shares are down 37% since, even as revenue kept growing.

cards.name: Life360
cards.why: Makes a mobile app that helps families track each other's location and stay safe. Lauren Antonoff took over as CEO in August 2025 after founder Chris Hulls moved to executive chairman, and this quarter's results missed estimates by 57%. The stock is down 37% since, but revenue keeps climbing.

cards.name: Arteris
cards.why: Licenses interconnect technology for semiconductor chip design. New CFO Saurabh Sinha stepped in this August, succeeding the retiring Nick Hawkins, right as the company missed earnings estimates by 67%. Shares have dropped 29% since, while revenue continues to grow at a healthy clip.

cards.name: StubHub
cards.why: Runs an online marketplace for buying and selling live event tickets. Analysts had modeled a profit for the latest quarter; the company came in at breakeven instead, a complete miss, and shares have fallen 25% since, though revenue is still climbing.

cards.name: Vishay Precision Group
cards.why: Makes precision measurement and sensing technology components for industrial and test markets. Earnings came in 79% below what analysts expected, and the stock has slid 38% since. Revenue, notably, hasn't slowed down.

cards.name: Core Scientific
cards.why: Runs data centers for bitcoin mining and AI computing infrastructure. The second quarter's loss came in far wider than analysts had modeled, and shares have fallen 16% since, even as revenue more than doubled year over year. Director Eric Weiss bought 7,000 shares on the open market on August 18, 2026.

cards.name: Hut 8 Corp
cards.why: Runs data centers for AI and bitcoin mining. The second quarter's loss ran well beyond what the Street had priced in, and the stock has fallen 18% since, even with revenue up 81% year over year.

cards.name: VF Corporation
cards.why: Makes and sells outdoor, active, and work apparel brands including Vans, The North Face, and Timberland. Abhishek Dalmia took over as CFO in August 2026 after Paul Vogel's departure, and the latest quarter missed estimates by 23%. Shares are down 29% since, while revenue is only down modestly, not collapsing. CEO Bracken Darrell bought shares on the open market on July 31, 2026, two days after the report.

cards.name: ATS Corporation
cards.why: Runs automated manufacturing and assembly systems. Doug Wright took over as CEO in January 2026 after Andrew Hider's abrupt departure the year before, and the first quarter fully under his leadership missed estimates by 14%, a fairly classic leadership reset. Shares have fallen 31% since, while revenue is down only modestly. Wright also bought shares on the open market in March 2026.

cards.name: Knife River
cards.why: Mines aggregates and produces ready-mix concrete, asphalt, and other construction materials. Earnings missed by 32% this quarter, and the stock has dropped 31% since, while revenue is still growing.

cards.name: ESAB Corporation
cards.why: Makes cutting, welding, and gas control equipment for industrial fabrication. New CFO Brent Jones stepped in this May, succeeding the departing Kevin Johnson, right as the second quarter came in just 4% below estimates, a fairly modest miss. Shares have still fallen 28% since, though revenue kept growing at a healthy double digit clip.

cards.name: BillionToOne
cards.why: Makes molecular diagnostics tests. The company missed earnings estimates by 38% this quarter, and shares have fallen 26% since, while revenue is still growing quickly.

cards.name: LeMaitre Vascular
cards.why: Makes medical devices for treating peripheral vascular disease. CFO Dorian LeBlanc joined in March 2025, and the company's latest quarter missed estimates by a modest 9%. Even so, shares are down 25% since, while revenue has kept growing.

cards.name: Tennant Company
cards.why: Makes industrial cleaning equipment for maintaining floors and surfaces in commercial and industrial spaces. The company missed earnings estimates by 37% this quarter, and the stock is down 24% since, while revenue has held roughly flat. Director Donal Mulligan bought 8,000 shares on the open market on August 12, 2026.

cards.name: Dick's Sporting Goods
cards.why: Runs a chain of sporting goods stores that recently absorbed the Foot Locker acquisition. This quarter missed estimates by 9%, largely because the newly acquired Foot Locker business underperformed and the company cut its guidance for that unit. Shares fell 31% since the report. Revenue is up sharply year over year, but that's the acquisition, not organic growth. Multiple directors bought a combined $3.7 million of stock on the open market on August 26 and 27, 2026, days after the report.

cards.name: Trade Desk
cards.why: Runs a programmatic ad buying platform. Its finance seat has turned over three times in under a year: a CFO who left after six months, an interim replacement, and now a third hire who started in July. Earnings missed by 8% this quarter, and shares are down 19% since. CEO Jeff Green has bought roughly $300 million of stock on the open market in two rounds, in March and April 2026, among the largest insider purchases in the industry.

cards.name: La-Z-Boy
cards.why: Makes and sells residential upholstered furniture through its La-Z-Boy Furniture Galleries stores. Earnings missed estimates by 12% this quarter, and shares have dropped 28% since, while revenue is down only modestly, not collapsing.

cards.name: Trinity Industries
cards.why: Runs railcar leasing and manufacturing for the North American rail industry. The company missed estimates by 7% this quarter, and shares have fallen 22% since, while revenue is down only modestly.

cards.name: Powell Industries
cards.why: Makes custom engineered electrical power distribution equipment. This was a narrow miss, just 3% below estimates, but shares still fell 19% since the report, even as revenue kept growing.
